description: The grouped bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks across various language families. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "family," and displays nine language groups: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, arranged generally in alphabetical order with Indo-European (IE) sub-families grouped first. The vertical axis represents the value, labeled "effect," using a linear scale with visible tick marks and corresponding horizontal grid lines at 0, 10, 20, and 30, indicating a tick interval of 10. Within each language family category on the horizontal axis, the chart displays a group of six adjacent bars representing different models or configurations, as indicated by the legend. From left to right within each group, the bars represent mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). Every bar is outlined in black and features a vertical black error bar with caps, indicating variability. The bar heights vary significantly across categories and models, with some extending below the zero line. The tallest bar is the mBERT-B₂ (light pink) configuration in the IE-Indic family, reaching an approximate value of 24, with its upper error bar extending past 30. The lowest value is seen in the mBERT-R₂ (light green) bar within the Semitic family, which drops to approximately -3. The Isolate and Uralic families consistently show the lowest overall effect values, with all bars remaining near or below 2. Conversely, the IE-Indic family exhibits the highest overall values, particularly for the mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂ configurations, which range from approximately 18 to 24.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family. The horizontal axis displays categories labeled as language families, including IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, arranged sequentially from left to right. The vertical axis is labeled 'effect' and ranges from 0 to 40, with intervals of 5 units. Each category contains six bars representing different models or configurations: mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂, colored light blue, dark blue, light green, dark green, pink, and red, respectively. Notably, the Semitic group shows the highest variability, with error bars spanning from approximately -10 to 25, while the IE-Indic group consistently exhibits the largest effect values, peaking at around 30. In contrast, the Uralic group demonstrates the lowest effect values, with all bars below 5. The IE-Germanic group shows a steady increase across configurations, while the IE-Baltic group displays a slight decline in effect values across models. Error bars indicate the standard deviation, highlighting variability within each language family and model configuration.
